title: Think aloud while solving a coding problem (B2)
summary: Nói to khi giải bài code: nhắc lại đề, nêu ví dụ, chọn hướng giải, độ phức tạp và các trường hợp biên.
learningObjectives: Nhắc lại đề bài và ví dụ trước khi viết code
Giải thích hướng giải và độ phức tạp

sections.title: Coding prompt
sections.content: Synthetic training artifact — non-production. Interview: Software Engineer, Marlowe Data. Interviewer: Given a list of user IDs, return the IDs that appear more than once. Please think aloud while you work. Notes: restate the problem, try an example, choose an approach, state time and space cost, then test edge cases.

vocabulary.technicalMeaning: Mức thời gian hoặc bộ nhớ thuật toán cần khi dữ liệu lớn dần.

vocabulary.technicalMeaning: Đầu vào hiếm hoặc cực đoan có thể làm hỏng lời giải.
vocabulary.example: An empty list is an edge case.

vocabulary.technicalMeaning: Đi qua từng phần tử của một tập dữ liệu.

performanceTask.title: Think aloud through one problem
performanceTask.scenario: The interviewer gives a coding problem and asks you to talk through your thinking before and while you code.
performanceTask.baselinePrompt: Think aloud in English for about 90 seconds: restate the problem, try an example, choose an approach, state its complexity and test one edge case. Do not look at the model answer yet.
performanceTask.performancePrompt: Speak in English for about 90 seconds: restate the problem, give an example, explain your approach and its complexity, and test one edge case.
performanceTask.modelResponse: Let me restate the problem to make sure I understand: I need the user IDs that appear more than once in a list. For example, with one, two, two, three, the answer is two. A simple approach would be comparing every pair, but that costs quadratic time, which is too slow for a large list. I can improve this by using a set to remember the IDs I have seen. As I iterate over the list once, I check each ID. If it is already in the set, I add it to the result, and otherwise I store it. That brings the time down to linear, with extra space for the set. Let me check an edge case: an empty list should return an empty result, and an ID that appears three times should be returned only once, so I would keep the result in a set too. Finally, I would write a few tests, including a list with no duplicates. Does this approach sound reasonable before I start coding?
performanceTask.retryPrompt: Think aloud again in English. Keep the same order and make your complexity statement clearer.
performanceTask.transferPrompt: Think aloud through a different problem, such as finding the first non-repeating character.
performanceTask.reviewPrompt: Think aloud through a new coding problem without looking at old notes.

rubric.label: Order of thinking
rubric.description: The candidate restates, exemplifies, chooses, states the cost and tests.

anchors.met: The listener follows all steps in order before the code starts.
anchors.notMet: The candidate starts coding or skips the restatement.

rubric.label: Complexity and improvement
rubric.description: A simple approach and an improvement are compared.

anchors.met: States the cost of the first idea and why the better idea is faster.
anchors.notMet: Gives the final idea without explaining the cost.

rubric.label: Edge cases
rubric.description: At least one edge case is tested aloud.

anchors.met: Names a specific input such as an empty list and the expected result.
anchors.notMet: Says "I would test more" without any case.
